name: Kishotenketsu (four-part twist)
summary: Introduce, develop, twist with an unexpected angle, then reconcile into a new understanding; no conflict required.
references: Classical East Asian four-part composition (Chinese qi-cheng-zhuan-he, Japanese kishotenketsu)
title_style: Calm descriptive titles, under 10 words; the twist title should surprise.

sequence.purpose: Ketsu: reconcile the two into new insight.

pitfalls: Forcing conflict into it; the twist is a new angle, not a fight.
A twist so unrelated it never reconnects.
Explaining the twist before it lands.

example.topic: A fictional office finding a use for server-room heat
outline: Our office plants are watered every Monday
They grow well, slowly, by the windows
Meanwhile, the server room runs warm all week
We moved the plants beside the servers; both thrive
Waste in one place can be fuel in another
